---
title: Vectors
icon: Sparkles
description: "A managed vector store: create indexes, upsert embeddings with metadata, and run cosine, dot-product or euclidean similarity search for semantic and RAG features."
---

import { Search, Database, Boxes, Code2 } from 'lucide-react';

Vectors is a managed store for embeddings. You create a **vector index**,
**upsert** vectors alongside the document ids and metadata they represent, and
**query** by a vector to get the nearest matches ranked by similarity. It powers
semantic search, recommendations and retrieval-augmented generation, and lives
under `/v1/vectors` in the same project as everything else.

<Callout title="You bring the embeddings">
Applad stores and searches vectors; it does not generate them. Produce your
embeddings with a model of your choice (OpenAI, a local model, whatever), then
upsert the numeric arrays here. An index records a `model` label and
`dimensions` for your own bookkeeping, but no embedding is computed server-side.
</Callout>

## Create an index

An index fixes the vector space: its `dimensions` and its distance `metric`.
Give a `name`; `indexId` is optional.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Node.js', 'Python', 'cURL']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await client.vectors.createIndex('docs', 1536, { metric: 'cosine', name: 'Docs' });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```ts
await server.vectors.createIndex('docs', 1536, { metric: 'cosine', name: 'Docs' });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
client.vectors.create_index("docs", 1536, metric="cosine", name="Docs")
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="cURL">
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/vectors/indexes \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"indexId":"docs","name":"Docs","dimensions":1536,"metric":"cosine"}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Underlying route: `POST /v1/vectors/indexes`. `name` is required. Defaults:
`dimensions` 1536, `metric` `cosine`, `model` `text-embedding-3-small`. The
response is the index:

```json
{
  "$id": "docs",
  "name": "Docs",
  "dimensions": 1536,
  "metric": "cosine",
  "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
  "status": "ready"
}
```

The `metric` decides how similarity is scored:

| Metric | Score | Higher score means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cosine` (default) | cosine similarity | vectors point the same way |
| `dot` | dot product | aligned and large-magnitude |
| `euclidean` | `1 / (1 + distance)` | closer in space |

List, fetch and delete indexes with `listIndexes()`, `getIndex(id)` and
`deleteIndex(id)` (`GET /v1/vectors/indexes`, `GET` and
`DELETE /v1/vectors/indexes/{indexId}`). Deleting an index removes its vectors.

## Upsert vectors

Upsert takes an array of vectors, each with an `id`, its `values` and optional
`metadata`. Re-upserting the same `id` replaces it.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Python', 'cURL']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await client.vectors.upsert('docs', [
  { id: 'doc-1', values: embedding1, metadata: { title: 'Intro', url: '/intro' } },
  { id: 'doc-2', values: embedding2, metadata: { title: 'Setup' } },
]);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
client.vectors.upsert("docs", [
    {"id": "doc-1", "values": embedding1, "metadata": {"title": "Intro"}},
    {"id": "doc-2", "values": embedding2, "metadata": {"title": "Setup"}},
])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="cURL">
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/vectors/indexes/docs/vectors \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"vectors":[{"id":"doc-1","values":[0.01,0.02],"metadata":{"title":"Intro"}}]}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Route: `POST /v1/vectors/indexes/{indexId}/vectors`. A single vector can also be
written with `PUT /v1/vectors/indexes/{indexId}/embeddings/{docId}` (body
`vector` plus `metadata`). Delete with `deleteVectors(id, ids)`
(`POST /v1/vectors/indexes/{indexId}/delete` with an `ids` array) or one at a
time via `DELETE /v1/vectors/indexes/{indexId}/embeddings/{docId}`.

## Query by similarity

Query with a vector to get the nearest documents. `topK` caps how many come
back; `scoreThreshold` drops anything below a similarity you set.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Node.js', 'Python', 'cURL']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
const res = await client.vectors.query('docs', queryEmbedding, { topK: 5 });
for (const hit of res.hits) {
  console.log(hit.documentId, hit.score, hit.metadata);
}
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```ts
const res = await server.vectors.query('docs', queryEmbedding, { topK: 5 });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
res = client.vectors.query("docs", query_embedding, top_k=5)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="cURL">
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/vectors/indexes/docs/query \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"vector":[0.01,0.02],"topK":5,"scoreThreshold":0.7}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Route: `POST /v1/vectors/indexes/{indexId}/query`. `topK` defaults to 10 (max
1000). The response is the ranked hits:

```json
{
  "total": 2,
  "hits": [
    { "documentId": "doc-1", "score": 0.91, "metadata": { "title": "Intro" } },
    { "documentId": "doc-2", "score": 0.82, "metadata": { "title": "Setup" } }
  ]
}
```

<Callout title="How search runs, and its limits">
Similarity search is computed in-process by scanning every vector in the index
and scoring it against your query. That is simple and dependency-free, and fine
for a self-hosted store up to roughly 100k vectors per index; beyond that a
dedicated vector database is the better fit. Metadata filtering is not applied
by the query engine yet, so filter client-side on the returned `metadata`.
</Callout>

## A minimal RAG loop

The store gives you the retrieval half of retrieval-augmented generation:

1. Embed each source document and `upsert` it with the text (or a pointer to it)
   in `metadata`.
2. At question time, embed the question and `query` the index for the top matches.
3. Feed the retrieved `metadata` into your model's prompt as context.

Applad handles steps 1 and 2's storage and ranking; you own the embedding model
and the generation call.
